structured_output.summary: The PR adds a size-bounded LRU cache (`src/cache/lru.ts`) in front of `getPrice` so repeated lookups for the same SKU stop reaching the pricing service, and a test file (`test/cache/lru.test.ts`) covering hits, misses and eviction. The cache is wired in at one call site (`src/pricing/get-price.ts:18`) and sized from `PRICE_CACHE_SIZE`, defaulting to 500 entries. The change does what the description says for the common path; the remaining issues are in how recency and expiry are tracked, and one test that does not reach the behaviour it is named for.

intent.note: Both claims in the description are present: lookups go through the cache at src/pricing/get-price.ts:18, and the size bound is read from `PRICE_CACHE_SIZE` with a default of 500 at src/cache/lru.ts:12. The description's "entries expire after five minutes" is implemented as `ttlMs = 300_000` at src/cache/lru.ts:14.

findings.title: Overwriting an existing key does not refresh its recency, so a hot key can be evicted first
findings.explanation: `set` updates the stored value in place when the key already exists but never moves the entry to the most-recently-used end of the map. A key that is written often and read rarely therefore keeps its original insertion position and is the first to go when the cache fills, which is the opposite of what an LRU promises. `get` does re-insert the key (line 44), so the two paths disagree about what "recently used" means.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:58-63 — `if (this.map.has(key)) { this.map.get(key)!.value = value; return }` updates in place
src/cache/lru.ts:44-46 — `get` deletes and re-inserts the key, moving it to the newest end
src/cache/lru.ts:66-68 — eviction removes `this.map.keys().next().value`, the oldest insertion
test/cache/lru.test.ts:40-52 — no case writes the same key twice before filling the cache

findings.title: A capacity of 0 from a mistyped environment variable silently disables the cache
findings.explanation: `PRICE_CACHE_SIZE` is parsed with `Number(...)` and only checked for `NaN`. A value of `0` (or a negative number) passes the check, and the eviction loop then removes every entry immediately after it is written, so every lookup misses and goes to the pricing service. Nothing logs that the cache is effectively off.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:57 — `if (Number.isNaN(capacity)) throw ...` is the only validation

findings.title: Expired entries are returned by `get` until something else is written
findings.explanation: Expiry is checked only inside `set`, when the eviction loop runs. `get` returns whatever is stored without comparing `expiresAt` to the clock, so on a read-heavy path a price can be served long after the five minutes the description promises, for as long as no new key is written.
evidence: src/cache/lru.ts:64-70 — the only `expiresAt` comparison is in the eviction loop inside `set`

findings.title: The eviction test fills the cache to exactly its capacity, so nothing is ever evicted
findings.explanation: The case named "evicts the least recently used entry" creates a cache of size 3 and writes three keys, then asserts that the first is gone. With exactly three writes the cache never exceeds its capacity, so the assertion can only pass if eviction runs one entry early — which is what the off-by-one in the eviction loop does. The test currently passes for the wrong reason and would fail if that loop were corrected.
evidence: test/cache/lru.test.ts:31-38 — `new LruCache(3)` followed by three `set` calls and `expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined()`
src/cache/lru.ts:66 — `while (this.map.size >= this.capacity)` evicts when the map is full, not over-full
findings.suggestion:
const cache = new LruCache<string, number>(3)
  cache.set('a', 1)
  cache.set('b', 2)
  cache.set('c', 3)
  cache.set('d', 4)
  expect(cache.get('a')).toBeUndefined()

inconclusive.question: Does the cache stay within the memory budget the description quotes for a full cache of production-sized price records?
inconclusive.what_would_settle_it: Running `pnpm bench:cache` against a fixture of real price records at `PRICE_CACHE_SIZE=500`. The records in `test/fixtures/prices.json` are a few hundred bytes each, which would put a full cache well under the quoted budget, but the production records carry a tier table that the fixture omits.

inconclusive.question: Is `PRICE_CACHE_SIZE` set in the deployed environment, or does production run on the default?
inconclusive.what_would_settle_it: The deployment's environment configuration, which is not in this checkout. `.env.example` does not list the variable, so the default of 500 is the likely value.
